questions.question: Explain about a Gray Hat Hacker.
questions.solution_html:
• Grey hat refers to an individual who operates without malicious intent but still violates
  • laws or acceptable standards of behavior by exploiting security vulnerabilities without
  • permission. Grey hat hackers exist between white hat and black hat hacking.
  • Explanation – (1 mark)

questions.question: Discuss about the different types of hackers.
questions.solution_html:
• White Hat, black hat, grey hat, blue hat, red hat, green hat, script kiddies, hacktivists
  • state/nation sponsored hackers etc.
  • Identifying different types, brief explanation – (1 mark)

questions.question: Compare hacking and ethical hacking.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare hacking and ethical hacking.
  • Hacking is unauthorized intrusion into computer systems and networks, often with
  • malicious intent. Ethical Hacking, on the other hand, involves similar techniques but is
  • conducted with legal authorization and aims to identify and rectify security
  • vulnerabilities. While hacking is criminal, illegitimate and unfavourable, ethical hacking
  • is legal and favorable to enhance security.
  • Comparison – (1 mark).

questions.question: Describe the term “Vulnerability”.
questions.solution_html:
• A vulnerability is a weakness in an IT system that can be exploited by an attacker to deliver
  • a successful attack. They can occur through flaws, bad coding/features, user error or a
  • combination of these.
  • Explanation – (1 mark)

questions.question: Explain cyber attack.
questions.solution_html:
• Cyber attacks are deliberate attempts by threat actors to gain unauthorized access to
  • systems, steal sensitive data, disrupt operations, or damage digital infrastructure. These
  • attacks can target individuals, businesses, or governments and often exploit weaknesses
  • in software, human behavior, or system configurations.
  • Explanation – (1 mark)
  • Protocols and explanation – (1 mark) each

questions.question: Explain Malware attacks.
questions.solution_html:
• A malware attack is a cyberattack where malware (malicious software) executes
  • unauthorized actions on the victim's system. The malicious software encompasses many
  • specific types of attacks such as ransomware, spyware, command and control, and more.
  • Definition – ½, explanation – ½

questions.question: Explain input validation attacks.
questions.solution_html:
• Input validation attacks are a method of cyberattack in which the attacker injects
  • malicious input that can be interpreted and executed by a target system to exploit its
  • vulnerabilities.
  • Definition – ½, explanation – ½

questions.question: Explain botnets.
questions.solution_html:
• A botnet is a network of infected devices (bots) controlled remotely by an attacker
  • (botmaster) through a Command and Control (C&C) system.
  • Explanation – (1 mark)

questions.question: Compare hardware firewall and software firewall.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare hardware firewall and software firewall.
  • A software firewall is a special type of software that runs on a computer/server to secure
  • it malicious attempts. A hardware firewall is a dedicated appliance. It has its own
  • processors, memory, and interfaces built solely for inspecting and controlling traffic.
  • Comparison – (1 mark)

questions.question: Identify an Example for Hardware Firewall.
questions.solution_html:
• Cisco ASA, SonicWall Network Security Appliances, PaloAlto Networks series etc.
  • Identify – ½, brief explanation – ½
questions.final_answer: Cisco ASA, SonicWall Network Security Appliances, PaloAlto Networks series etc

questions.question: Discuss about the purpose of maintaining access to a compromised / system.
questions.solution_html:
• The purpose of maintaining access to a compromised system (often called persistence) is
  • to ensure that an attacker—or, in ethical hacking, a security tester—can continue to
  • interact with the system even after the initial breach – continuous control, monitor target
  • activities, achieve privilege escalation, launching further attacks etc.
  • Maintaining access definition – (1 mark)
  • Purpose explanation – (4 marks)

questions.question: Describe the different techniques used to clear tracks.
questions.solution_html:
• “Clearing tracks” refers to actions taken after a compromise to hide evidence of
  • unauthorized activity and avoid detection. The various techniques invlolve Log
  • Manipulation or Deletion, File and Artifact Removal, Timestamp Manipulation
  • (Timestomping), Clearing Command-line History, Use of Anti-Forensic Tools, Rootkits and
  • Hidden Processes, Disabling Security Mechanisms, Obfuscation and Encryption, Clearing
  • Network Traces etc.
  • Definition – (1 mark)
  • Identifying and explaining different techniques – (4 marks)

questions.question: Discuss about Man-In-The-Middle attacks.
questions.solution_html:
• A man-in-the-middle (MITM) attack is a cyberattack in which a hacker steals sensitive
  • information by eavesdropping on communications between two online targets. Instead of
  • User ↔ Server, MITM uses User ↔ Attacker ↔ Server.
  • Stages in MITM attacks – Interception, Decryption, Manipulation, Relaying.
  • Common Techniques Used in MITM - ARP Spoofing, DNS Spoofing, Session Hijacking etc.
  • Definition – (1 mark)
  • Stages – (1 mark)
  • Common Techniques – (1 mark)
  • Detection methods – (1 mark)
  • Prevention methods – (1 mark)

questions.question: Explain Buffer overflow attacks. List out some consequences of buffer / overflow attacks.
questions.solution_html:
• A buffer overflow attack occurs when a program writes more data into a memory buffer
  • than it can hold. Because buffers have fixed sizes, extra data “overflows” into adjacent
  • memory, potentially overwriting critical information.
  • Consequences - Arbitrary Code Execution, System Crashes, Privilege Escalation, Data
  • Corruption, Unauthorized Access, Malware Injection, Compromise of Entire System etc.
  • Definition – (1 mark)
  • Consequences - (4 marks)

questions.question: Discuss about the methods used to protect websites.
questions.solution_html:
• Use Secure Communication (HTTPS), Input Validation and Sanitization (to prevent SQL
  • injection, XSS etc.), Strong Authentication & Authorization (use of strong passwords
  • MFA), Web Application Firewall, Regular Updates and Patch Management, Secure Session
  • Management, Regular Security Testing, Backup and Recovery Plan, Logging and
  • Monitoring, Secure Configuration.
  • Any 5 methods and explanation – (1 mark) each

questions.question: Describe the process of authorization and explain the different types of / authorization techniques.
questions.solution_html:
• techniques.
  • Authorization is the process of determining what actions an authenticated user or service
  • is allowed to perform.
  • Types of Authorization Techniques - Discretionary Access Control (DAC), Mandatory
  • Access Control (MAC), Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), Attribute-Based Access Control
  • (ABAC), Rule-Based Access Control, Access Control Lists (ACLs).
  • Definition – (2 marks)
  • Types identification – (2 marks)
  • Types explanation – Any 4 types – (4 marks) each ((16 marks))

questions.question: Differentiate between HIDS and NIDS.
questions.solution_html:
• HIDS (Host-Based Intrusion Detection System) and NIDS (Network-Based Intrusion
  • Detection System) are security tools used to detect malicious activities, but they differ in
  • where and how they monitor.
  • HIDS is installed on individual systems (hosts) to monitor internal activities like file
  • changes, logs, and processes.
  • NIDS is placed on a network to monitor traffic flowing between devices and detect
  • suspicious patterns.
  • Differentiate in terms of location, monitoring, scope, detection, performance, deployment
  • etc.
  • HIDS definition – (2 marks), explanation – (8 marks)
  • NIDS definition – (2 marks), explanation – (8 marks)
